claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, each LMT battery, EV battery and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the EU market or put into service must have a battery passport; batteries placed earlier are not made passport-equipped by that rule.

The regulation reserves individual state-of-health, status and use-history data for persons with a legitimate interest and limits commercially sensitive access; the Commission's current implementation timeline places the battery access-rights implementing act in Q4 2026.

For a waste industrial, EV or LMT battery to cease being waste after preparation for reuse or repurposing, Article 73 requires state-of-health evidence, documented further use and protection against transport damage; Annex XIV separately requires evidence when shipping a used rather than waste battery.

Producers or producer-responsibility organisations must take back waste industrial and EV batteries free of charge and route them to permitted treatment, so owner-paid waste routing cannot be the core paid event.

The IEA reports that second-life economics remain challenged by safety, warranty, uncertain remaining life, dismantling and repurposing costs, liability transfer and falling new-battery prices, while used and end-of-life battery flows remain early and uncertain.

Direct incumbents already offer substantially the proposed workflow: Cling publicly describes fixed-fee inventory assessment, success-based transaction advisory and logistics orchestration, while Circunomics markets condition analytics, passport-ready documentation and B2B battery trading.

Poland's installed storage base is growing: URE reported 102,066 grid-connected stores at or below 50 kW at end-2025, and a government programme selected 172 large stores planned by end-2028; these are installed-base indicators, not near-term retirement volume.
Polish counterparties' authorized waste-management scope can be checked in BDO, and a 2026 road inspection of lithium-ion batteries documents that ADR paperwork errors are actively enforced.

contrary_evidence: EU producer-responsibility rules require free take-back of waste industrial and EV batteries, directly undermining an owner-paid compliant-waste-routing fee.
Battery passports apply only to covered batteries placed on the market or put into service from 18 February 2027, so early retirement events and legacy stock may have no passport.
The detailed access-rights act is still shown by the Commission for Q4 2026; lawful downloadable and reusable fields cannot yet be assumed.
The IEA finds second-life reuse economically difficult and says future used-battery flows remain uncertain and may arrive later than expected.
Cling and Circunomics already combine assessment, qualified buyer matching, documentation and logistics support across Europe.
Poland's fast-growing installed base is recent, so it does not establish enough retirement events in the first three years.

economics.acquisition_route: Secure non-binding first-notice pilots from five installers, then dry-run documentation on ten known future replacement or repowering events with a permitted recycler and qualified second-life buyer; explicitly compare every case with the free producer/EPR take-back route
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 8-12 year scenario: 2,500 annual unit or batch dispositions at 2,500 PLN blended net revenue yields 6.25m PLN revenue; 25% operating profit at 4x implies 6.25m PLN enterprise value and 5m PLN for an 80% founder stake. It depends on paid non-waste transactions or contracted programme administration, not charging for statutory free waste take-back.
economics.founder_time: 10-16 hours per week for intake data, routing decisions and partner coordination; testing, hazardous-goods logistics, waste possession and treatment remain with credentialed partners
economics.gross_margin_basis: No inventory, transport or waste possession is included; software and documentation can be reused, while partner testing, legal classification, insurance and transaction execution remain variable costs
economics.payback: Unknown. The original 18-30 month target is not evidenced and must be tested against sparse early retirements, free producer take-back, failed-sale rates and partner costs before being used
economics.pricing: Revised unvalidated hypothesis: 500-2,500 PLN only for optional independent diagnostics/documentation that creates decision value, plus 8-15% of a completed lawful non-waste sale or a programme-administration fee paid by an installer/producer partner. Do not charge an owner merely to access statutory free waste take-back.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installers can generate repeat notice flow and buyers may return for consistent evidence, but free EPR routes and incumbent exchanges limit retention unless contracted first-notice coverage is real

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Contracted forward feedstock visibility plus permissioned condition, classification and realized-route outcomes improve routing decisions; restricted passport data is not sold, reused or processed beyond the authorized service
fingerprint.customer: Commercial battery owners and solar or storage installers needing an independent retirement decision, with qualified second-life operators, remanufacturers and permitted recyclers as counterparties
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed first-notice and first-inspection clauses into installer maintenance and repowering contracts, then route through permitted recyclers, ADR carriers and qualified second-life firms
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: First-notice intake, passport or source-document check, partner testing, product-versus-waste evidence pack, compliant buyer matching and auditable handoff; optional diagnostic fee plus success fee only for accepted lawful non-waste transactions or contracted programme administration
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The owner or installer pays only for an optional independent decision/evidence service; a qualified buyer pays a disclosed success fee after accepting a lawful non-waste unit or batch, while waste take-back follows the free producer/EPR route
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Warranty replacement, site repowering, lease end, capacity fade, insurer request, failed unit or an installer receiving first notice of decommissioning

founder_fit: Combines battery-health data, renewable-sector access and quantitative residual-value decisions
The no-inventory, no-transport pilot limits downside within available capital
Installer contracts could create recurring supply without consumer brand building
AI can assist document matching and state-of-health triage while classification, safety and transport decisions remain expert-led
The family-business channel is relevant but provides no verified customer, feedstock right or permission to use company resources
risks: A battery classified as waste triggers strict possession, storage, transport, treatment and shipment rules
Fire, injury, environmental and chain-of-custody liability can exceed transaction revenue
Producer/EPR free take-back can eliminate owner willingness to pay on waste routes
Battery-passport access is role- and purpose-limited, not exclusive, and may be unavailable for legacy batteries
Existing European brokers and marketplaces already possess buyer networks and transaction experience
Residual values and second-life demand may collapse as new battery prices and chemistries change
Recent Polish installations may not retire soon enough to support an early business
First-notice clauses may be unobtainable without guarantees, service obligations or revenue sharing

structure.control_point: Contractual first-notice and first-inspection rights over future retired batteries plus permissioned condition, classification and disposition records
structure.critical_dependency: Installers must grant prospective notice rights, partner testing must distinguish a lawful non-waste route from waste, and qualified demand must exceed testing, logistics and compliance costs despite free producer take-back

thesis: Research-stage hypothesis: sign installers and commercial battery owners to first-notice and first-inspection agreements for replacements, repowering and retirement events. Use owner documents, lawful battery-passport access where available and independent partner testing to decide between continued use, preparation for reuse or repurposing, remanufacturing and permitted recycling, without taking title, transporting or possessing waste. Battery passports cannot be the initial feedstock moat because they apply to post-February-2027 market placements and access remains purpose-limited. The paid wedge is an independent evidence pack and successful lawful non-waste match; statutory waste take-back must remain free through producers or producer-responsibility organizations. Contracted forward visibility, not passport-data resale, is the defensible asset.
title: First-Look Exchange for Retired Commercial Batteries
uncertainties: How many actionable commercial retirement events can five installer partners actually identify in the first three years
Whether installers grant first-notice or inspection rights without a guarantee, floor price or service-level commitment
Which passport fields the final Article 77(9) implementing act permits this operator to download, share or reuse
Testing cost and evidentiary standard for product-versus-waste classification by chemistry and use case
Share of units with positive non-waste value after partner testing, packaging, ADR logistics and buyer discount
Who pays for independent triage when producer/EPR waste take-back is free
Whether a Polish local wedge can compete with incumbent European exchanges and brokers
Insurance coverage and contractual liability allocation
